title: Control provenance scratchpad - Samir
content:
Purpose: quick scratchpad to map where evidence for key controls actually comes from (provenance), what’s manual, and low-effort automation options. NOT formal — working notes for Samir + quick sync with Maya/Lena.

High-level goals:
- inventory 8–12 candidate controls we expect to use for SOC2 (access, key mgmt, deployment gating, alerting, incident response, change review, backup verify, logging/retention).
- for each: record current evidence sources, owner, retention, test frequency, pain points, automation idea.
- identify 3 quick wins to reduce manual evidence collection (scripts, dashboards, retention policy links).

Quick glossary/assumptions:
- "evidence" = artifact we can hand to auditor (logs, runbook, policy doc, playbook execution output, console screenshots).
- retention baseline = 12 months unless otherwise noted.
- owners = product area + SRE on-call rotation.

Candidate control snippets (raw):
1) Control: MFA enforced for all admin accounts
   owner: identity squad / Maya Chen
   evidence source: Okta org -> System Log export filtered by eventType: user.mfa.method.verify
   current state: semi-manual export once per quarter; scripts exist but not scheduled
   retention: Okta logs retention = 90 days (gap)
   gap: auditors expect >= 12 months; we rely on backup to S3 that’s not consistently tagged
   automation idea: schedule daily export to secure S3 bucket with lifecycle rule; DID: INFRA-4123 references script; link PR to ops-scripts
   quick test: run scheduled lambda to fetch logs for last 365d -> sample 30 events -> package as evidence ZIP

2) Control: Key rotation + KMS access review
   owner: platform-cryptography / Samir Patel
   evidence source: KMS key policy snapshot, rotation_schedule docs, KMS audit logs (CloudTrail)
   current state: rotation implemented for service keys; some customer-managed keys on Dedicated not covered
   gap: dedicated/on-prem key rotation runbooks live in private repo (need sanitized export)
   automation: add Conformity check + monthly rotation report (CloudTrail query -> table)

3) Control: Deployment change approvals (PR gating)
   owner: release-eng / Lena Park
   evidence source: GitHub branch protection rules + PR review history; Jenkins pipeline run logs
   current state: branch protection OK; manual sign-off for infra changes still via Slack thread
   gap: sign-off artifacts exist but scattered (Slack + PR comments) -> auditor wants single consolidated trail
   automation: require CODEOWNERS + enforce status check that references approval ticket; archive approval messages to Confluence page via bot

4) Control: Backup verification
   owner: infra-backup / TBD
   evidence: periodic restore tests in staging (runbook outputs), S3 bucket inventory
   current: weekly backup created, restore test ad-hoc, no standardized evidence ZIP
   gap: inconsistent restore logs; no timestamped signed result
   automation: add a scheduled restore smoke test that outputs a signed JSON with checksum + timestamp and pushes to evidence S3 path

5) Control: Logging & retention for inference requests (privacy + forensics)
   owner: serving-runtime / infra-observability
   evidence: request logs (ELK), Audittrail index, retention policy doc in Confluence
   current: logs shipped to ES with 90d retention; large volume => cost pressure
   gap: need sampling strategy + proof of sampling; must redact PII before handing to auditor
   idea: implement daily sampled export (1%) for 365d retention in cheaper storage; include redaction step in pipeline

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Do we accept compressed summarized evidence (e.g., aggregated counts + sample rows) for high-volume logs vs full raw logs? (ask external auditor)
- For Dedicated customers with on-prem KMS, is our responsibility to provide rotation evidence or just our processes for how we request/customer provides evidence? (legal?)
- Which controls are scoped out for the first SOC2 run (critical path)? propose: identity, change mgmt, backups, incident response, logging. Others deferred.

Quick wins (3):
- Build scheduled Okta -> S3 export job (1 day dev + infra review). Ticket INFRA-4123.
- Add a nightly CloudTrail query to produce KMS access report -> push to evidence store (small lambda).
- Create a tiny "approval archiver" bot for Slack that records a sign-off message to Confluence with PR link (PoC by Lena).

Evidence packaging checklist (working):
- canonical filename pattern: redwood_evidence_<control>_<YYYYMMDD>_<owner>.zip
- manifest.txt inside ZIP: control-id, owner, evidence-files list, extraction instructions, redaction notes
- retention tag: evidence/2026/soc2/periodic

Risks / friction points:
- storage costs if we keep raw logs for 12+ months; need sample vs full retention decision.
- cross-org owner ambiguity (platform vs infra vs product). Keep escalation path documented.
- on-prem customers create special-case evidence flows and delays. Document as exceptions in scope doc.

Next steps / near-term TODOs:
- [ ] Sync with Maya on Okta retention workaround (blocker). Target: 2026-03-17.
- [ ] Samir: prototype CloudTrail KMS report -> PR (due: 2026-03-19).
- [ ] Lena: draft approval-bot spec and small scheduled demo (due: 2026-03-22).
- [ ] Create Confluence stub: CONF-NEW-control-evidence-index and link here.

Notes to self:
- keep notes short; this doc will be the ephemeral coordination artifact. Move matured mappings to Confluence page and tag owner.
- call out sample evidence sets early in auditor convo to avoid surprises.

References / quick links:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/pages/CONF-4821-control-framework (high-level)
- Jira: INFRA-4123 (Okta export), SEC-2201 (evidence retention discussion)
- GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-scripts/pull/88 (skeleton export script)
- Slack: #trust-ops (thread: archive/okta-export)

End of scratchpad.
